subject: chemistry-2
question: Percent mass/volume (% w/v) is a concentration unit used frequently in health science laboratories. Which description matches this unit, and how much solute is in 1000 mL of a 0.9% w/v solution?

options.text: Grams of solute per 100 g of solution; 9 g of solute
Grams of solute per 100 mL of solution; 9 g of solute
Grams of solute per liter of solution; 0.9 g of solute
Milligrams of solute per 100 mL of solution; 9 mg of solute

explanation:
Percent mass/volume is defined as grams of solute per 100 mL of solution, so 0.9% w/v supplies 0.9 g per 100 mL, and 1000 mL contains 0.9 g x 10 = 9 g. Choice A describes percent by mass (% w/w), which uses 100 g of solution rather than 100 mL, and choice D misassigns the mass unit as milligrams. Because laboratory and clinical fluids are measured out by volume rather than weighed, % w/v is the practical labeling unit for them.

ELI-10: Percent means per hundred, and the w/v version pins that hundred to 100 mL of finished solution while the solute is counted in grams. So 0.9% w/v translates to 0.9 g in every 100 mL. One liter is ten of those 100 mL portions, giving ten helpings of 0.9 g, or 9 g total. The mismatch between grams on top and milliliters on the bottom is deliberate and is the single thing that separates % w/v from % w/w, which weighs both parts.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
